title: Inspect and extend: Local persistence and the screen flow
objective: Use the real implementation in `src/exposureContext.tsx` to demonstrate and safely improve provider lifecycle, asyncstorage adapter, resources screen, reusable controls, and tabs.
problem: The provider is a shared notebook service for screens. Follow app startup through storage load, check action through update, and persistence save; inspect the resource screen and error/corrupt-data fallback behavior. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `src/exposureContext.tsx` and the related project files: src/exposureContext.tsx; src/store.ts; src/persistence.ts; src/screens/ResourcesScreen.tsx; src/components.tsx; src/theme.ts; App.tsx.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to provider lifecycle, asyncstorage adapter, resources screen, reusable controls, and tabs.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: History stays on the device in this demo; local storage is not a protected health record system.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: The provider is a shared notebook service for screens. Follow app startup through storage load, check action through update, and persistence save; inspect the resource screen and error/corrupt-data fallback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `src/exposureContext.tsx`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
